text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Tuesday.

GERMANY - German Bunds and futures deepened their losses in late trade on Tuesday. Analysts said the market was being dogged by fresh EMU concerns after the first round of French elections produced a swing to the political left at the weekend, opening up the prospect of a less strict interpretation on EMU entry rules.
The June Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 100.76, down 0.24 from Monday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - UK government bond (gilt) futures fell with other international bonds amid fgenerated by the surprise Socialist performance in the first round of the French elections. The June long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 112-12/32, down 3/32 from Friday's settlement price.
FRANCE - French bond futures came under pressure from a second wave of selling by non-residents on Tuesday but recovered with Bunds, partly on the back of domestic demand for bonds.

Traders said the decision by Prime Minister Alain Juppe to resign whatever the outcome of the second round of voting on June 1 was seen as positive for the centre-right and some were expecting the ruling coalition to scrape home.
The June bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 128.46, up 0.16. from Monday's settlement price.
ITALY - Italian debt markets recovered at the close after nervousness over the strong showing by France's Socialists had a delayed impact on London and U.S. traders back from a long weekend.

"After the initial nervousness the market calmed," one broker said noting Bunds had recovered, helping Btps and futures to close near the day's highs. The June bond future on LIFFE was trading at 129.95 up 0.05 from Monday's settlement price.
UNITED STATES - The prices of U.S. Treasury securities opened narrowly range bound on Tuesday as traders returned to their desks following the three-day Memorial Day weekend in the U.S.

Analysts expected little price movement this week as little substantive data was set for release. The June Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 108-21/32, down 17/32 from Friday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 7.04 percent.

JAPAN - Key June JGB futures contract ended lower on Tuesday in response to poor results of the four-year JGB auction and option-linked selling, traders said. In after hours trading the June future on LIFFE was trading at 123.17, down 0.49 from Monday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
EUROBONDS - Two countries tapped the mark sector for the first time on Tuesday. Slovenia raised 300 million marks and Lebanon 250 million.
A seven-year bond from the Republic of Slovenia -- rated A3 by Moody's Investors Service and A by Standard and Poor's Corp -- was priced to yield 43 basis points over the 6.75 percent Treuhand.
